model_output.verdict: A customer success manager with a clear account portfolio and a few unanswered questions about renewals.
write_up: Your resume tells a clear story: you moved from customer support into customer success at Brightline Payroll Software, where you manage mid-market accounts. A recruiter can see the customers and the work, though your part in renewal strategy needs more detail.

The 48-account portfolio is a strong model for the rest: it names the customers and how many accounts you manage. The onboarding checklist also stands out because you built something the whole CS team now uses.

Start with the at-risk renewal line and add what you contributed. Then give the payroll escalation work and the earlier client questions a little more detail. You don't need a number on every line; you need enough for a recruiter to understand the job you did.

cards.line: - Manage a book of 48 mid-market accounts across healthcare and manufacturing
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It gives a recruiter both the kind of accounts you own and the scale of the portfolio without making them guess.

cards.line: - Partnered with Sales on renewal strategy for at-risk accounts
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see who you worked with, but not what you contributed to the renewal strategy or what happened to the accounts.
cards.example: Partnered with Sales on renewal strategy for at-risk accounts by [your contribution], resulting in [renewal result]
cards.question: What did you contribute to the strategy, and what happened with those renewals?

cards.line: - Handle escalations with Support and Product when payroll runs fail
cards.cannot_tell: Failed payroll runs are an important customer problem. What part did you handle with Support and Product, and what happened next?
cards.example: Handle escalations with Support and Product when payroll runs fail by [your role], helping [result]
cards.question: What do you handle during a payroll escalation, and what results can you point to?

cards.line: - Answered client questions by phone and email
cards.cannot_tell: The channels are clear, but the questions could cover a lot. Naming what clients came to you for would show more of your insurance work.
cards.example: Answered small business client questions about [types of questions] by phone and email
cards.question: What kinds of questions did those clients ask you?

fit.note: Your experience points most clearly toward customer success work with B2B software accounts. The support background and payroll escalations add a useful customer-service foundation.
